key_insight: GBClaw connects agentic AI workflows with atomistic simulations to reveal how defect hierarchies and metastable grain-boundary structures influence sliding resistance.
engineering_relevance: The framework could help researchers investigate interface-controlled deformation and inform microstructure design in polycrystalline materials.
method: Coordinate LLMs, specialized agents, domain tools, simulation interfaces, and hierarchical memory.
Dynamically replan simulations and refine workflows for targeted mechanistic analysis.
Compare boundary sliding with and without secondary misfit dislocations, then perform researcher-guided follow-up calculations.
evidence_signal: Across 14 general asymmetric tilt grain boundaries in nickel, GBClaw identified diverse deformation modes and substantial shear-strength differences associated with secondary misfit dislocations.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to the studied nickel boundaries, and resolving anomalous behavior required researcher-guided follow-up.
paper_title: GBClaw: An agentic AI framework for atomistic grain boundary research and mechanistic discovery
